To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy requirement of Holstein heifers or steers at the age of 6 mo was greater (NEm of 0,57 MJ/kg BW 0,75) than the commonly accepted values for adult dairy cattle and that methane emission from these cattle was 6,8% of GE intake.

the energy use efficiency of 6-mo-old dairy cattle (Holstein) is greater than the values for adult dairy cattle and the methane emissions from 6-mo old dairy cattle are higher than the commonly accepted values for adult dairy animals.
the NEm of 6 mo Holstein cattle was 0.57MJ/kg BW0.5 and methane energy output was 0.068MJ/kg GE intake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the energy metabolism and methane emissions of young Holstein cattle at age of 6 mo.
the development of a model to predict enteric CH4 emissions in dairy cattle.
the development of a new method to predict the energy intake, energy use efficiency and methane emission in dairy and beef cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there was no significant difference between heifers and steer cattle in terms of enteric methane emission rates and efficiency of use energy at the age of 5 to 6 mo.

the data from this study indicate that the NEm of 6-mo-old dairy cattle is greater than that of adult dairy cattle and that methane emissions from 6-moold cattle are greater than the commonly used values for adult cattle.
the data from the present study can be used as a reference point for future studies on young stock of dairy cattle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data from this study can be used to estimate the energy requirement and methane production of dairy and beef cattle at 6 mo old.
the methane energy output was greater than the accepted value of 0.065 for adult cattle.
there is a need to improve the prediction of energy requirement in young dairy stock, and that the current methane emission inventories are overestimating methane emissions from young dairy stock.
The main takeaway from our work is that
methane emissions are greater than previously reported for cattle of this age and that the energy requirement for maintenance is greater than previously reported in the literature.
methane energy output is greater than the value used to develop methane inventories for dairy cattle, and this needs to be addressed in the future.

the maintenance energy requirement for 6-mo-old Holsteins was 1.2 times greater than that for 6-m0-old Friesians and 1.5 times greater than that of 6-mo old Angus steers, whereas methane emissions from 6-mo Holsteins were 1.3 and 1.4 times greater than those of Friesians and Angus steers, respectively.
